## Natural history notes

A wingless velvet ant wasp characterized by a fuzzy, ant-like body with black and reddish-orange coloration and four pale spots or patches that give it the “four-spotted” appearance, while males are winged and more wasp-like. In Florida, the Four-spotted Velvet Ant is found in sandy open habitats such as scrub, sandhills, pine flatwoods, roadsides, fields, and forest edges where ground-nesting bees and wasps occur. Females search for host nests on the ground and lay eggs near developing bee or wasp larvae, with the velvet ant larva feeding as a parasitoid; females can deliver a very painful sting and should be observed without handling.
